items.title: Phasmophobia Resonance update adds Dowsing Rods to help find the bone
PHASMOPHOBIA RESONANCE UPDATE LAUNCHES WITH UNITY 6, NEW GHOST HUNTING EQUIPMENT AND MAJOR GAMEPLAY IMPROVEMENTS!
items.summary: Ghost hunters are in for another major upgrade as Kinetic Games officially launches Resonance, the latest free content update for its hugely popular cooperative psychological horror game, Phasmophobia.
items.content:
Available from 24 November 2026 across all supported platforms, Resonance combines the game’s transition to Unity 6 with a substantial content update, introducing new ghost hunting equipment, improved voice recognition, enhanced graphics, accessibility features and significant quality-of-life improvements.

The update represents another important milestone in Phasmophobia’s development as Kinetic Games prepares for the highly anticipated full 1.0 release.

Following the game’s recent achievement of surpassing 30 million sales worldwide , Resonance demonstrates the developer’s continued commitment to expanding and refining the paranormal horror experience.

One of the biggest additions arriving with Resonance is the introduction of Dowsing Rods, an optional piece of investigation equipment designed to help players locate the Bone during contracts.

The new equipment should prove particularly useful when exploring larger and more challenging locations, including Brownstone High School, where locating the Bone can become a time-consuming task.

Dowsing Rods are available across three equipment tiers, offering increasingly accurate information:

The addition gives ghost hunters another strategic tool to utilise during investigations, particularly when exploring Phasmophobia’s more expansive haunted environments.

Resonance also introduces significant changes to the existing Sound Sensor, making it easier for players to monitor paranormal activity from the safety of their investigation truck.

A redesigned map interface now distinguishes between ongoing and individual sounds, providing investigators with more useful information about activity inside haunted locations.

Looping sounds remain visible for a period of time, while individual noises appear as a single ping before disappearing.

The improved system can also help experienced players identify certain ghost types by monitoring their movement speed, potentially opening up new investigation strategies for teams.

Speaking directly to ghosts has always been one of Phasmophobia’s most memorable features, and Resonance is expanding those interactions even further.

The updated Voice Recognition system introduces additional recognised phrases, allowing players to request specific paranormal interactions during investigations.

Players who prefer using Text mode will also benefit from a new dedicated Journal page listing the available phrases.

items.title: How to use Dowsing Rods in Phasmophobia
items.summary: Finding the bone has never been easier. The post How to use Dowsing Rods in Phasmophobia appeared first on Destructoid.
items.content:
Gaming How to use Dowsing Rods in Phasmophobia Destructoid Follow Kacee Fay Tue, November 24, 2026 at 12:06 PM UTC Tue, November 24, 2026 at 12:06 PM UTC figure]:grid max-md:[&>figure]:grid-cols-article-mobile max-md:[&>figure>*]:col-fullbleed max-md:[&>figure>figcaption]:col-body"> *]:pointer-events-auto hidden md:block"> Screenshot by Destructoid The Resonance update has officially landed in Phasmophobia , bringing with it an entirely new piece of ghost-hunting gear to try out. The Dowsing Rods are quite unlike anything else in your collection, making them a bit of a tricky item to use.

There are no other equipment items capable of doing what the Dowsing Rods can, so figuring out how to make use of this key item is essential. If you're struggling to work with this item, here's how to use Dowsing Rods in Phasmophobia .

Make sure you go and check out our sister site, GTA 6 Bible , for all your GTA 6 needs.

The Dowsing Rods are a directional navigation tool that can be activated to help you track down the bone in Phasmophobia . While holding this tool, you can follow the guidance it provides to help you pinpoint where to look for the bone. They're mainly designed to be used on larger maps , but work anywhere.

The better the Tier of the Dowsing Rods, the easier they are to use for finding it. Regardless, though, the overall way they work remains the same across all three Tiers, so here's a full breakdown of how to use them.

Purchase Dowsing Rods from the shop. This item is not part of the base ghost hunting equipment gear pool, so you must manually purchase and add them yourself to have access to this tool during a contract. You can add up to two Dowsing Rods to your truck loadout.

Load into any map. Once you've got Dowsing Rods added to your collection, head to any location to use them. For your first attempt, you might consider making a custom mode where the ghost can't kill you so you can freely learn how to use this tool without any worries.

Grab the Dowsing Rods. You can find them hanging up on the equipment wall right above the Flashlights and under the Ghost Writing Books.

Stand still while holding the Dowsing Rods. Head inside any map, hold the Dowsing Rods in your hand, and stand completely still. Watch their movement to gain insight as to where the bone is. The rods only work when you're still, so stopping frequently to use them is crucial.

Find a spot where the Dowsing Rods cross or point up/down. When the rods cross, you're pointed in the rough general direction where the Bone is located. Move in that direction and check again consistently as you hone in on where it is. If the rods point up or down, you're right above or below the bone, so head in the direction they're hinting to find it.

Keep searching until the Dowsing Rods stay permanently crossed. Once you're in the correct room, the rods will cross to let you know. For Tier I and Tier II, they'll stay permanently crossed no matter what, so it's up to you to hunt around the room to find the bone. For Tier III, they'll only cross when you're looking in the right direction, allowing you to find the precise location of the bone with ease.

The Dowsing Rods' main ability is to point toward the bone on the map. This is their primary function and use, which means they work best when you use them for this purpose.

They do also have a secret bonus ability , though, which is to detect the ghost during a hunt. This tool highlights the exact direction the ghost is in an increased radius that's a bit bigger than the range of detection for bones. It's about 25 meters for Tier I, 30 meters for Tier II, and about 40 meters for Tier III. This feature also means you cannot find the bone during a ghost hunt, as the rods are instead locked onto the ghost.

Made out of wood and copper, and can be used to guide you in the general direction of the bone. Not super accurate or reliable, but with some patience, it can help you get the job done.

items.title: Phasmophobia v0.20.0.0 - Resonance Patch Notes
items.summary: Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. Today, we have released the Resonance update for Phasmophobia. The update is now available across all platforms where Phasmophobia is available. If you encounter any issues in downloading the update, or followin
items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters.

Today, we have released the Resonance update for Phasmophobia. The update is now available across all platforms where Phasmophobia is available. If you encounter any issues in downloading the update, or following, please do contact us via our Help Centre.

Below, you’ll find details on what is included in the Resonance update, or you can head to our recent Development Preview for more information.

New: 

  • Unity 6: The move to Unity 6 brings with it improvements across the board for Phasmophobia including performance, stability, lighting and more. Phasmophobia also now supports various different quality presets for in-game systems and different platforms such as Steam Deck. Importantly, this update brings with it a host of bug fixes, all of which can be found below.

    [/*]

  • Performance Improvements & New Options: Unity 6 and its accompanying features has improved Phasmophobia’s performance and stability through notable changes. Resonance addresses commonly encountered crashes, improves CPU, GPU, VRAM and RAM usage as well as allowing for new overall quality presets. Elsewhere, a new Extreme shadow setting for compatible hardware has been added and an option to turn off/on the Live Camera Feed (for Photo & Video Cameras) is now available. Note: If Live Camera Feed is turned off, the Media highlight will still appear on the Camera.

    [/*]

  • Lighting Improvements: As detailed in the recent Development Preview, Resonance brings with it an overhaul to the overall lighting system in Phasmophobia. These changes will be notable during all weather types where darker areas of a location will be lit through windows and doorways, and outside areas will be brighter. Areas of improvement also cover lighting on dynamic objects such as props and doors; originally, an interactable would be lit in a different way to others whereas now these will blend with the rest of the environment.

    [/*]

As this lighting change is game-wide, we'll be looking out for any and all feedback via our Help Centre to help us continue to improve and refine it.

  • Voice Recognition Improvements & Changes: In Resonance, we've made additions to Voice Recognition to allow for a more immersive experience with new options allowing players the chance to ask for interactions or proof of presence from the Ghost. An additional page in the Journal has been added too, listing off various line options. These new options replace the ability to say certain words or the Ghost’s name to try and increase Ghost activity.

    [/*]

  • Sound Sensor Map: Once a Sound Sensor has been placed down inside a location, an icon on the Truck’s map will reflect the type of sound as and when it happens. These will ping differently depending on if the sound is a single sound or a looping sound. A sound can only be picked up if it is happening within the range of the Sensor itself.

    [/*]

  • Dowsing Rods: The Dowsing Rods are a new piece of Equipment used to locate the Bone during any Contract. Designed mainly for use on larger maps, the Dowsing Rods will point players towards the Bone, with higher tiers providing better accuracy such as which floor the Bone can be found on.

    [/*]

  • Map Voting: The Map Voting system has been reworked to allow for a more customised approach for players. Players are now able to select as many maps as they wish to create their own random map pool. Buttons on the Contract board can be used to select all small, medium and large maps separately as well as a randomiser that works in the same way as the original Random polaroid did.

    [/*]

  • Colour Blind options: Various different Colour Blind options are now available. These can now be found within the Settings > Video menu and support the following types of colour blindness: Protanopia, Protanomaly, Deuteranopia, Deuteranomaly, Tritanopia, Tritanomaly, Achromatopsia, Achromatomaly.

    [/*]

  • In-Game Warnings: As we continue to improve the overall experience for players in Phasmophobia, a new Warning system has been implemented. Initially, these will provide warnings for violations of our Code of Conduct, but we’ll continue to evolve this system as we go. If action is taken against a report, the player who made the report will now receive a notification informing them that it has been successful.

    [/*]

  • XBOX Play Anywhere: Phasmophobia is now available as part of the XBOX Play Anywhere program, allowing players to play the game across the devices that support XBOX - PC, laptops, ROG Ally and XBOX Series X/S. Save data will carry across your devices, meaning you can switch between any XBOX system and retain your progress.

    [/*]

  • Console language support - Additional language support for PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X/S has been added. The following languages are now supported on all platforms: English, German, French, Italian, Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Polish, Romanian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Swedish, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Catalan, Arabic, Spanish (Latin America), Portuguese (Portugal), Spanish (Spain), Portuguese (Brazil).

    [/*]

  • Eye Adaptation: A new Eye Adaptation setting, Performance, has been added for all players, including VR. The previous On option is now changed to Quality. Note: VR and low end hardware only support the Performance setting.

    [/*]

Changes:

  • Ghost Changes

    • A Yurei’s normal interactions with doors are now slightly faster than other Ghost types.

      [/*]

    • During a Hunt, a Yurei moves doors faster than other Ghost types.

      [/*]

items.title: Phasmophobia Resonance update arrives November 24 as free Unity 6 transition
items.summary: Phasmophobia's free Resonance update lands November 24, adding ghost voice commands, Dowsing Rods, a Sound Sensor rework, and a Unity 6 engine transition.
items.content:
Phasmophobia’s free Resonance update is set to arrive tomorrow, November 24 , and its headline feature upgrades the game’s voice recognition so players can command ghosts to interact with nearby objects.

Talking to the dead has always been Phasmophobia’s signature mechanic. The co-op horror hit from Kinetic Games asks players to speak aloud to identify and provoke the entity haunting each map, and equipment like the Spirit Box works only when players address the ghost directly. The Resonance update builds on that foundation: reportedly, the improved voice recognition will let a player ask ghosts to “throw things” , a description from Eurogamer, deepening the two-way exchange between hunters and hunted instead of just provoking a response.

Resonance is also a technical milestone. The update reportedly transitions Phasmophobia to Unity 6, bringing better performance and sweeping bug fixes, alongside new Dowsing Rod equipment in three tiers, with Tier 3 the most useful for finding a Bone during an investigation. The Sound Sensor, long among the game’s least-used tools, gets a reworked interface with more accurate information, and future updates are slated to improve character customization and rework the 42 Edgefield Road map as part of the game’s long path to a 1.0 release.

Phasmophobia has been in early access since launching on Steam in September 2020, and it has kept a large, active player base since. The Resonance update will be free for all owners.

items.title: Phasmophobia Resonance Update Moves Game to Unity 6 on November 24, Performance Gains Unproven
items.summary: Phasmophobia Resonance update arrives November 24 as a free release that moves the co-op ghost-hunting game to Unity 6 and adds Dowsing Rods, a reworked Sound Sensor map and Xbox Play Anywhere. Kinetic Games expects fewer crashes and lower memory use, but players cannot verify those performance
items.content:
Share on WhatsApp Kineticgames.co.uk Kinetic Games will release Resonance , a free Phasmophobia update , on Tuesday, November 24, moving the four-player co-op horror game to the Unity 6 engine and adding Dowsing Rods, a new tool for locating the Bone. The studio announced the date on November 17, and the update covers PC via Steam, PS5, PS VR2 and Xbox Series X|S. The release gives no launch time, so the update could go live at any point on the 24th.

For players, the engine swap is the part to watch. Kinetic CEO Daniel Knight calls the move to Unity 6 "a technical upgrade first and foremost," and the performance and stability gains the studio describes are expectations, not measured results. If you play on a lower-end PC, a console or a VR headset, the patch notes due at launch will show what changed.

The press release says Unity 6 brings more realistic lighting and better stability, along with fixes for several prominent bugs raised in recent community feedback. New settings arrive with it: expanded graphics and quality options, a VR Eye Adaptation setting and color-blindness accessibility options. PlayNews counts eight color-blind modes and also lists graphics presets and an extreme shadow-quality option.

The migration was already late. Kinetic's 2026 roadmap targeted October for the Unity 6 upgrade and promised a new lighting system with it. A later patch post moved the target to November, a slight delay from October. Development Preview #22, published November 2 , then merged the engine move with a content update that was meant to ship separately, according to PlayNews coverage .

Kinetic expects lower CPU, GPU, VRAM and RAM use and says it has fixed memory leaks, according to PlayNews's coverage of the Development Preview. The same report says some common crashes are already fixed in the Unity 6 build.

Independent confirmation does not exist yet. Jeu.video reports that the developer expects fixes and improvements but that real performance gains can only be judged after release . Player.one likewise notes that the improvements have not been tested publicly .

Unity 6 launched on October 17, 2024 , with improved graphics rendering among its changes. Two of its rendering features map onto what Kinetic promises. The GPU Resident Drawer uses Unity's BatchRendererGroup API to draw objects with GPU instancing, which reduces draw calls and frees CPU time. It works only with Forward+ and on graphics APIs that support compute shaders, and it lengthens build times. Unity's Mathieu Muller told 80 Level that some scenes saw more than double the performance, thanks to the Drawer or to Unity's Spatial Temporal Post-Processing upscaler, a vendor claim that depends on the scene.

On the lighting side, Adaptive Probe Volumes place light probes automatically based on geometry density, in bricks of 64 probes arranged in a 4×4×4 grid, to build baked indirect lighting. Kinetic says Unity 6 allowed major lighting improvements , but it has not said whether it uses either feature. Any player-side benefit would depend on which features the studio enabled and whether a given device supports them.

Engine migrations also carry risk. Unity's upgrade guide for Unity 6.0 for moving a project from 2022 LTS lists changes that can affect existing projects, including a change to how physics torque is computed for some force modes. Kinetic has not said which Unity version Phasmophobia ran before or whether any such change touched its code. The game's technology stack also includes IL2CPP, the Burst compiler, Steam Audio, Vivox voice and OpenXR, according to SteamDB's detected technologies list , so a new engine version touches a lot of moving parts.

For anyone new to the game: one to four players take a contract to work out which type of ghost haunts a designated site. Your team of paranormal investigators loads equipment into a van, enters a building and records evidence that is sold on to a ghost removal team. The central question is which ghost you are dealing with, and whether your team can identify it before it turns on you. PC Gamer's review described the experience as one of restraint and subtlety, a detective game about ghosts that left the reviewer and companions rattled and talking for hours. Kinetic calls the new Dowsing Rods especially useful on large maps such as Brownstone High School, where finding the Bone is a bigger search.

Dowsing Rods are new equipment for finding the Bone rather than the ghost room. Better tiers give more accurate readings: Tier 1 gives a general direction, and Tier 3 tells players which floor the Bone is on.

Real dowsing has a poor record. It is classed as pseudoscience , and the ideomotor effect, small unconscious movements, is the explanation usually given for why rods move. Controlled tests, including a 1948 trial of 75 dowsers, have generally found no ability beyond chance. In Phasmophobia , the rods are an equipment tier system with stated accuracy levels, not a divination claim.

The reworked Sound Sensor map separates ongoing sounds from one-off sounds with icons, and the map can help identify a ghost by its movement speed. The limit: it only identifies sounds on the player's current floor .

Voice recognition now covers more requests. Players can ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches or to throw nearby objects, and a list of usable phrases will appear in the Journal. The commands also work in text voice-recognition mode, but Player.one notes Kinetic has not said ghosts will always respond to the commands . Voice recognition and voice chat problems were still listed as known issues across platforms earlier this year, according to The Escapist.

items.title: Phasmophobia's next update adds Dowsing Rods to hunt for bones, and lets ghosts throw things on command
items.summary: Phasmophobia’s free Resonance update lands on 24th November, adding Dowsing Rods, new voice commands, custom map pools, and a move to Unity 6.
items.content:
Image credit: Kinetic Games News by Vikki Blake Contributor Published on Nov. 21, 2026, 3:56 p.m. Follow Phasmophobia Prioritise us on Google Phasmophobia 's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

You'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and new buttons let you quickly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," said Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive."

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2 , although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association , more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027 , as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update , admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

items.title: Phasmophobia's next update lets you tell ghosts what to do, and it has a release date
items.summary: Phasmophobia's next major update will let ghost hunters ask spirits to interact with doors, switches and nearby objects. Kinetic Games has confirmed that
items.content:
This article needs JavaScript to display. Please turn on JavaScript in your browser and reload the page. Phasmophobia's next major update will let ghost hunters ask spirits to interact with doors, switches and nearby objects. Kinetic Games has confirmed that the free Resonance update arrives on November 24 across the game's current platforms.

There is much more than a new list of things to shout into a microphone. The update introduces dowsing rods for finding the Bone, changes the sound sensor and moves the game to Unity 6, alongside lighting improvements and bug fixes.

VR players are included in those changes. Kinetic has also explained how the new commands will work if you use text-based voice recognition, so you do not have to rely on a microphone to try them.

A promotional screenshot from Phasmophobia. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

In its development preview , Kinetic says the expanded recognition system will let players ask ghosts to interact with nearby doors and switches, throw objects or give a sign of their presence. The journal will list the usable phrases.

Those options will be available through text recognition as well. For VR players using text mode, the developer says the commands will be accessible on the sanity watch.

That should make it easier to know what you can actually ask, instead of guessing through an investigation. Of course, having a new command is not a guarantee that a ghost will cooperate.

An existing-game screenshot; Kinetic says Resonance will improve lighting. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

The new dowsing rods are intended to help locate the Bone, particularly on large maps such as Brownstone High School. Tier 1 points towards a general direction, while the higher tier can narrow the location down to a floor.

Kinetic is also reworking the sound sensor's map interface. It says icons will distinguish ongoing sounds from one-off noises, and players will be able to use movement speed as one clue when identifying a ghost. The sensor only identifies sounds on the same floor as the player.

There is also a custom random map pool: players can choose which locations the game selects from and use shortcuts for small, medium or large maps.

Full patch notes are expected when Resonance launches. Image: Kinetic Games / Steam

Kinetic says the engine transition is intended to improve stability and performance, and it expects to address crashes and other bugs. Those are the developer's expectations; the studio says it can judge the performance change properly once players have the update.

Resonance also adds lighting changes, new quality settings and an eye-adaptation option for VR. The studio's release-date announcement says full patch notes will arrive when the update launches.

items.summary: Welcome back, Ghost Hunters. We want to start this Development Preview, which contains a lot of exciting news for the rest of the year, with a heartfelt thank you to those that have continued to support us throughout this year. The feedback
items.content:
Welcome back, Ghost Hunters.

We want to start this Development Preview, which contains a lot of exciting news for the rest of the year, with a heartfelt thank you to those that have continued to support us throughout this year. The feedback you’ve provided us has helped us shape Phasmophobia in the last few months and in what’s to come. 

After our Roadmap shift earlier in the year, we committed to a more transparent style of communication with you and we intend to stick with that. You can expect to hear much more from us as we work towards Phasmophobia 1.0 in late 2027.

With that said, let's get into the details. With this Development Preview, we’re going to be talking to the following topics:

  • The upcoming Content Update.

    [/*]

  • Phasmophobia’s move to Unity 6.

    [/*]

  • New in-game warnings.

    [/*]

  • Phasmophobia on XBOX Play Anywhere.

    [/*]

  • Player Character Visual Update

    [/*]

  • 42 Edgefield Road Rework.

    [/*]

There’s a lot of information to dig into, so we highly recommend getting settled in with a warm cup of \ and a couple of biscuits.

Firstly;

Introducing the Resonance Update

While we’ve been working on multiple updates over the Summer, one thing became clear - shipping these at different times was looking unreasonable, both for us and you. So instead, we’ve packaged together the Unity 6 update and our Content Update into one. We’re calling this Resonance, and it’ll be launching in late November. 

We’ll dive into more detail on the move to Unity 6 shortly, but let’s talk about some new features coming to Phasmophobia as part of Resonance first.

Up first, the Dowsing Rods.

Icons on the Sensor’s map will reflect the type of sound - a looping sound will stick around for a while whereas a single sound will ping once and disappear. Only sounds on the same floor will be identified by the Sound Sensor. You’ll also be able to use the Sound Sensor’s map as a way of determining a Ghost type based on the speed of movement, which will be especially useful during a Hunt.

As part of this update, we’ll also be introducing a new aspect of Voice Recognition, giving you the chance to instruct the Ghost to interact with nearby objects such as doors and switches and take action such as throwing objects or give a sign of their presence. These options will also be available for players that have their Voice Recognition mode set to Text. For VR players using Text mode, these options will be available via the Sanity watch where they’ll be able to use these commands.

To make sure you can keep track of what’s possible with Voice Recognition, we’re adding the below page to the Journal, listing out the usable phrases - no more shouting into the void in the hope you get it right! 

Finally, before we move on, you’ll now be able to select as many maps as you wish to create your own random map pool. We've also added new buttons to quickly select small, medium and large maps. The fourth icon, the dice, will serve the same purpose as the original Random Map polaroid. And hey, by removing a polaroid from the board, we make room for newer additions. That’s helpful!

Our Transition to Unity 6

For a while now, we’ve been speaking about our move to Unity 6 - the latest version of the engine Phasmophobia runs on. We apologise it’s taken a while to get to this point, but we’re happy to say we’ll be making the leap over to Unity 6 as part of Resonance. 

The biggest part of Unity 6 is focusing on Phasmophobia’s stability, performance and improving the overall experience for Ghost Hunters. It’s also a futureproofing exercise, opening up a lot of potential for the game - especially in the run up to Phasmophobia 1.0 later next year and our plans beyond that point. 

Since we began work on this iteration of the game, a lot of the reported bugs have been fixed within the Unity 6 update of Phasmophobia. With the release of this update in late November, you can expect to see lots - and we do mean lots - of bug fixes, general improvements and more implemented into the game. While we’ll share patch notes on release, a lot of the more common issues we see players encountering will be addressed with this update, including the more common crashes players have been experiencing.

Unity 6 has also given us the ability to improve the lighting across the board in Phasmophobia, to create a much more realistic and immersive experience for Ghost Hunters. While this isn’t an update that’s immediately visible to the naked eye, the video and images below show the difference of what’s now possible.

Alongside the above lighting changes, we’re introducing several new Settings to improve your time with Phasmophobia, ranging from graphical settings presets, an extreme shadow quality setting as well as overall quality presets and Eye Adaptation for VR players. We’re also implementing the following accessibility options for players that experience colour-blindness;

  • Protanopia

    [/*]

  • Protanomaly

    [/*]

  • Deuteranopia

    [/*]

  • Deuteranomaly

    [/*]

  • Tritanopia

    [/*]

  • Tritanomaly

    [/*]

  • Achromatopsia

    [/*]

  • Achromatomaly

    [/*]

As mentioned, the move to Unity 6 aims to greatly improve the overall performance of Phasmophobia for all players across CPU, GPU, VRAM and RAM usage, while also fixing any memory leaks we were seeing. We’re expecting this to be a significant improvement, but one we can only truly gauge when the update is in your hands. Once the update is live, we’ll be closely monitoring any and all feedback to see where we can continue to make improvements, so please do submit any bugs you encounter to our Help Centre so our team can investigate.

New In-Game Warning System

One part of the road to Phasmophobia 1.0 that is important to us is improving the overall player experience in-game. We want to investigate ways for your time spent in-game with others to be more rewarding and meaningful, and vitally, feel like a part of a community.

While we'll share more of our thoughts and ideas at a later stage, one piece of this that we're introducing as part of the Resonance update is a new system in-game that provides player's with a warning message if they have been found to be in violation of our Code of Conduct instead of immediately resulting in a ban - unless of course their actions are severe enough to receive an immediate ban.

We'll also be informing you if a report you have made has resulted in action taken against a player you've reported.

XBOX Play Anywhere

Finally, as part of the Resonance update, we’ll also be introducing Phasmophobia into the XBOX Play Anywhere program. This means that if you own Phasmophobia on XBOX already, you’ll be able to play it across any device that supports XBOX play - PC, laptops, ROG Ally and of course, XBOX Series X/S.

For more details on how the XBOX Play Anywhere program works, head over to the official website.

The Resonance update is one of our biggest updates to date for Phasmophobia in terms of technicality and what it means for the game going forward. We’re excited to get it out to you and use it as a jumping off point for the next year’s worth of work, leading into Phasmophobia 1.0.

That said, there’s still more to come between now and then. To finish up, we wanted to share an update on our Player Character Visual Update as well as the next rework in line for release - 42 Edgefield Road.

Player Character Visual Update

Following on from our Player Character Update, we made the decision to add an extra update this year that focused on fleshing out the customisation and cosmetic side of Phasmophobia. With this we’ll be introducing over 30 new and unique cosmetics, each with their own colour and texture variants, improving the UI of the Customisation Shop and the character models themselves.

We had originally planned to ship this as part of the Resonance update, but we need to spend a bit more time on it to make sure it’s ready to make its way to you. Ultimately, we wanted to make sure Resonance is as solid and stable an update for everyone and this meant looking at each individual aspect and making the decision on what was ready, and what was not. 

We’ll share more details on when you can expect to see this update in Phasmophobia but in the meantime, we’re excited to share some screenshots of the upcoming cosmetics and UI rework as a preview.

42 Edgefield Road Rework

42 Edgefield Road is the next map in-line for a makeover, and our reworked version of it will be launching later this year. While we’ll share details on the rework closer to release, we wanted to leave you with a teaser in the form of the below screenshot.

Resonance will be launching for Phasmophobia next month, and we hope that the details we’ve shared in this Development Preview have you excited for its release. In the run up to the update, we encourage you to ask us questions via our social channels, our Discord server and Help Centre if you would like to know any more specifics about what we’ve talked about today. 

We’re excited to round out this year with really strong updates and believe it’ll put us in a good place heading into 2027 and beginning the road to 1.0 - which we’ll make sure you join us for every step of the way. 

Thank you, Ghost Hunters.

For those of you who have taken part in previous Crimson Eye events, you’ll know what to expect, but you’ll also get to see how Nell’s Diner and the reworked 6 Tanglewood Drive & 13 Willow Street look dressed in red. For newer Ghost Hunters, you’ll be tasked with hunting down Blood Moon totems and completing investigations and optional objectives to earn points, all while under the threat of Blood Moon weather, increasing the challenge you’ll face from ghosts.

Players will have several different unlockable rewards during the event: a seasonal event tee, the Beholder ID Card & Badge set and the Blood Moon charm.

Alongside these will be the upgradeable trophy. If you have previously unlocked this, you’ll continue to earn points and upgrades to your existing Trophy, rather than a new one.

During the event, we have a few different plans in place, so please do read on to learn what’s in store throughout October.

Twitch Drop

During the first week of Crimson Eye, a Twitch Drop campaign will be running for all Phasmophobia streamers. After watching a total of two hours of Phasmophobia streams, you’ll earn the Crimson Eye tee. The campaign will be live from the moment the event begins until 11:59 PM BST on October 15th, 2026.

Double XP & Rewards

As is becoming tradition with Phasmophobia’s seasonal events, we’ll be running a Double XP & Rewards event during Crimson Eye. This will be taking place between October 15th–22nd, with all rewards from completed investigations being doubled during this period. Mark your calendars, Ghost Hunters!

Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts with the American Heart Association

Finally, during the final week of Crimson Eye (October 26th–November 1st), we’ll be bringing back Ghost Hunts 4 Hearts with our friends over at the American Heart Association! Last year, the Phasmophobia community raised over $100,000, which was an incredible achievement and went a long way towards helping the AHA team with their important work.

This year, we’re planning to go bigger and better; this event, and its rewards, will be accessible to all Phasmophobia creators & players when it goes live. While we’ll share details nearer the time, we just wanted to get the dates in your calendars!

We look forward to celebrating our favourite season with you once again, Ghost Hunters.
